title: Electronic tuning of the soft-phonon transport anomaly in Ta$_2$Ni(S$_x$Se$_{1-x}$)$_5$
authors: Yuan-Shan Zhang, Masahiko Isobe, Hidenori Takagi, Dennis Huang
abstract: Ta$_2$NiSe$_5$ continues to be investigated for its phase transition at $T_\textrm{c}$ = 326 K, where it develops both an electronic gap and a distortion of its Ta/Ni chains. One intriguing feature at $T_\textrm{c}$ seen in thermal transport is the giant anisotropic scattering of phonons moving perpendicular to the chains, which is apparently associated with the softening of a transverse acoustic phonon, but whose microscopic origin and significance demand clarification. By tuning the normal-state band overlap/gap with S substitution, we uncover a close connection between this soft-phonon transport anomaly and underlying electronic instabilities: When Ta$_2$Ni(S$_x$Se$_{1-x}$)$_5$ approaches a band insulator at high $x$, and signatures of the electronic transition are suppressed, the soft-phonon transport anomaly concomitantly vanishes. Our results establish the following picture for the Ta$_2$Ni(S$_x$Se$_{1-x}$)$_5$ family: Near the S end, a sole lattice instability gives rise to a weak structural transition with $T_\textrm{c}$ approaching 130 K. Near the Se end, additional electronic instabilities boost $T_\textrm{c}$ up to 326 K and amplify experimental signatures of the transition. The strong interaction between electrons, holes, and the lattice is manifested as a soft-phonon transport anomaly accompanied by electronic fluctuations, which include excitonic and hybridization-gap fluctuations.
summary: This research investigates the phase transitions in Ta2Ni(S_xSe_{1-x})_5 by linking anomalous phonon transport to electronic instabilities. The authors demonstrate that the soft-phonon anomaly is not isolated but arises from a complex interplay involving excitonic, hybridization, and lattice fluctuations. This suggests that multiple correlated mechanisms must act together to stabilize the material's high critical temperature.
main_problem: To clarify the microscopic origin and significance of a 'soft-phonon transport anomaly' observed at a phase transition in Ta2Ni(S_xSe_{1-x})_5, and to establish the interplay between electronic instabilities and lattice dynamics.
main_result: The soft-phonon anomaly is strongly coupled to underlying electronic instabilities, suggesting that three types of interactions—excitonic, hybridization-gap, and intrinsic lattice instability—must coexist to explain the high transition temperature ($T_c$).
method: The study combines experimental measurements (thermal/electrical transport, heat capacity) with theoretical analysis comparing multiple competing instability mechanisms.
model_or_system: The physical system is the quasi-one-dimensional chalcogenide solid solution Ta2Ni(S_xSe_{1-x})_5. The investigation probes how tuning stoichiometry ($x$) modifies the interplay between electronic gaps and lattice softening.
key_observables: Soft-phonon transport anomaly (anisotropic phonon scattering), electrical conductivity ($\sigma$), thermal conductivity ($\kappa$), and the logarithmic derivative of conductivity ($\epsilon_{\parallel}$).
important_parameters: $T_c$ (ranging from $\sim 130 	ext{ K}$ to $326 	ext{ K}$), stoichiometry $x$, and electronic gap energies.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the observed anomalies are due to strong electron-phonon coupling, requiring consideration of excitonic, single-particle hybridization, and lattice instabilities simultaneously.
figures_summary: Figures show signatures of electronic gaps in $\epsilon_{\parallel}$ and magnetic susceptibility ($\chi$), alongside V-shaped suppression anomalies in perpendicular phonon diffusivity ($D^{(	ext{ph})}_{\perp}$) centered at $T_c$.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes transport measurements across the composition gradient, correlating the vanishing of the soft-phonon anomaly with the approach to a band insulator state. It culminates by proposing that only the simultaneous action of multiple instabilities can explain the high $T_c$ observed in $	ext{Ta}_2	ext{NiSe}_5$.
why_interesting: The work provides an excellent case study for understanding how lattice dynamics (phonons) are intimately coupled to electronic correlations and gap formation, a central theme in strongly correlated electron physics.
